title: Residual diagnostics and principled respecification
summary: When a model fits poorly, locate the misfit in the residuals and revise only for substantive reasons, never by following modification indices mechanically.

body.text: A poor global fit says something is wrong, not what. Residual correlations, the differences between observed and model-implied correlations, show where: a cluster of large positive residuals among items assigned to different factors suggests a missing factor or cross-loading (Kline 2016). A [[standardized-residual]] puts each covariance residual on a z-like scale.

A [[modification-index]] estimates how much χ² would drop if one fixed parameter were freed. Freeing parameters because their MI is large capitalises on chance: the modified models fit the sample but often do not replicate (MacCallum et al. 1992). Free a parameter only with a substantive reason, report it, and validate on new data.

SEM Lab reports SRMR, the summary of residual correlations, but does not yet show the residual matrix or modification indices. In the exported lavaan script, `residuals(fit, type = "cor")` and `modindices(fit)` provide them.
body.title: Not available in SEM Lab

body.text: In the starter, all eight items of the two-factor data are forced onto one factor: χ²(20) = 585, RMSEA = .238, CFI = .61, SRMR = .18. The principled response is to return to the instrument: the items were written for two facets, so a two-factor model is the theoretically motivated revision. It fits well (RMSEA = .013, CFI = .999). Adding error covariances until CFI exceeds .95 would also raise fit, but without meaning.

mistake.title: Correlating errors until the fit is good
mistake.text: Error covariances freed only because of large MIs are post-hoc patches. They make the model fit this sample and obscure the real problem, such as a missing factor.

tryIt.task: Run CB-SEM on this one-factor model and read the fit. Then rebuild it as two factors (v1–v4 and v5–v8, correlated) and run again.

checks.question: A modification index suggests a residual covariance between v3 (factor 1) and v6 (factor 2), and you have no substantive reason for it. What do you do?

options.text: Do not free it on that basis; examine the residual pattern and the theory of the items instead.
options.feedback: Correct. MI-driven changes without theory capitalise on chance.

options.text: Free it, since it improves fit significantly.
options.feedback: Almost any freed parameter improves fit in-sample; that is not evidence for it.
Deleting items to remove misfit is another data-driven change that narrows the constructs.

checks.question: What does a large positive residual correlation between two items tell you?

options.text: The model under-predicts their association: something they share is not in the model.
options.feedback: Correct. Observed minus implied is positive.
Unreliable items have low loadings; a residual concerns what the model fails to reproduce.
That would be a negative residual.
